title: Indirect Effect Estimation with Noisy Mediators and Finite Error-Calibration Samples
banked_reason: terminal:laundering — kernel_substituted@oeq:joint-frontier; promised exact joint and known-error frontiers remain open with a polynomial lower/upper gap.
gap_reasons: The TL;DR says the project determines the joint rate and derives precision-retention budgets, but both outputs remain open in the delivered statements.

The same-class known-error order is also unresolved, and the m proportional to n^(40/47) retention threshold is only a conditional algebraic consequence; the unconditional result supplies a weaker necessary budget condition.

The final Bessel and reconstruction lemmas require constructed-test geometry that has not been established for the actual variable mesh and tail complement, so they do not discharge the shared-gradient bottleneck.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery attempted the sharp two-budget frontier and obtained partial converse bounds, conservative honest procedures, and a consistency criterion. The actual variable-knot/tail calibration certificate and complete covariance/Hoeffding ledger remained open, leaving polynomially separated lower and upper rates and an unproved exact retention budget. D0.5 terminated on kernel substitution; no F-stage or Lean proof was reached, and the partial artifacts are preserved without frontier certification.
tldr: The precision of an interventional indirect mean depends jointly on cohort size and independent assay-error calibration. The focal object is the joint finite-budget estimation and honest-length rate \(r(n,m)\) for a continuous-mediator pathway observed through an unknown ordinary-smooth additive channel. Both latent arm densities and the nonlinear response remain unknown. The project determines that rate, constructs total data-only procedures with finite-sample full-class coverage, and derives the budgets retaining an independently justified same-class known-error order. A fixed equal-main-law pair supplies the zero-probe obstruction. The converse powers \(n^{-2/47}\) and \((1+m)^{-1/20}\), conservative finite-sample upper envelopes, and the uniform-consistency criterion are proved here. Matching upper powers, any logarithmic or mixed-budget corrections, and sharp tuning remain derivation tasks; the decisive analytical question concerns adaptive spatial reconstruction of the shared calibration gradient.
gap: Quadratic inverse-functional theory already establishes nonparametric exponents and noisy-operator effects. The inspected sources do not settle \(\int\nu-\int\nu f(P,0)/f(P,1)\) from complete Bernoulli-marked original records with arbitrary independent same-error probe budgets and finite-sample honest connected intervals.
fill: The named output \(r(n,m)\) must be justified by both lawful full-record converse constructions and an unconditional feasible upper certificate. The supplied-error comparison prices calibration, while the equal-main-law endpoint prevents population identification from being confused with a finite probe sample.
